 BTS Turn Singapore Into A Month-Long ‘Arirang’ Celebration With Concerts And Fan Experiences
 Nov 12, 2026 
 Facebook Twitter Pinterest WhatsApp Linkedin ReddIt Email Print 
 Prefer us on Google 
 Imagine an entire city celebrating your favourite band. Landmarks glowing red, drones dancing across the night sky, theme parks hosting exclusive parties and thousands of fans exploring a shared musical universe. That’s what BTS have planned for Singapore this December, transforming the island into an enormous celebration of their ‘Arirang’ era.
 The K-pop superstars have announced ‘BTS The City Arirang Singapore,’ a month-long collection of immersive experiences running December 1–31, 2026, alongside their four sold-out concerts at the National Stadium.
 For BTS ARMY, the celebration extends far beyond the concert stage.
 Created in collaboration with the Singapore Tourism Board, the project brings BTS-inspired installations, activities and entertainment to some of Singapore’s most recognizable destinations.
 From December 8–22, Marina Bay, bridges along the Singapore River and the famous Merlion will illuminate in Ari Red. The Asian Civilisations Museum and Peranakan Museum will also join the citywide transformation.
 The visual spectacle promises some extraordinary photo opportunities.
 Sentosa Island will host a three-night drone show and a special party, while Resorts World Sentosa becomes home to the official ‘Arirang’ Fan Village. Visitors can explore interactive challenges and themed Play, Taste and Beauty zones designed to bring the BTS experience into everyday activities.
 Universal Studios Singapore is getting involved, too.
 Its special ‘BTS The City Arirang Night Out’ will combine selected attractions, live entertainment, fan games, music and a themed fireworks finale.
 The festivities also reach Mandai Wildlife Reserve, where the Exploria attraction will receive a special BTS takeover.
 Across Singapore, 10 major destination partners will participate, including Gardens by the Bay, Jewel Changi Airport, National Gallery Singapore, National Museum of Singapore, New Bahru, The Kallang and Zouk Singapore.
 It’s an ambitious example of how a concert tour can become an experience for an entire city.
 The ‘BTS The City Arirang’ project began in Seoul before expanding internationally alongside the group’s world tour, with each destination developing experiences reflecting its own character.
 Singapore marks the project’s first and only Southeast Asian stop in 2026, closing its annual programming with its longest activation yet.
 For fans travelling to the concerts, the celebrations offer an opportunity to experience Singapore through music, culture, entertainment and shared excitement.
 BTS have built a global community that extends across languages and borders. Turning an entire destination into a celebration of that connection feels like a natural extension of their extraordinary reach.
 For 31 days this December, Singapore will be welcoming ARMY to a citywide celebration of BTS.
